title: Auto, taxi drivers to protest in Delhi today, demand fare hike and ban on bike-taxi apps

ai.summary: Auto and taxi drivers in Delhi plan protest on November 19 demanding fare hikes, banning bike-taxi apps, and reviewing EV policies, citing unfulfilled government promises.

facts.claim: Auto and taxi drivers in Delhi plan protest on November 19
facts.quote: Transport workers from across India will gather at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Wednesday, November 19, to demand higher auto and taxi fares, a ban on private bike-taxi services and a review of Delhi’s electric vehicle (EV) policy.
A key demand is an increase in auto-rickshaw and taxi fares.
The union has called for an immediate revision, along with a ban on private bike-taxi app services.
The transport union has sought a review of Delhi's EV policy, saying that the interests of auto and taxi drivers should be considered while framing regulations affecting the sector.
The union said the BJP government had been in power in Delhi for more than one and a half years but had not delivered on its promises to drivers.

ai.background_note: The protest involves transport workers uniting across states to demand fare revisions, bike-taxi curbs, and EV policy changes, highlighting unfulfilled government commitments.
